title: The Insane Story Behind Japan's First Supercar

scenes.text: In the early nineteen sixties, Japanese cars were widely seen as cheap and second-rate. A few years later, one of them broke thirteen world records in seventy-two hours, won races, starred opposite James Bond, and lost its maker money on every sale. This is the story behind Japan's first supercar, the Toyota 2000GT, and the places where our sources tell it differently.
scenes.caption: THE INSANE STORY BEHIND JAPAN'S FIRST SUPERCAR

scenes.text: Our sources are Wikipedia's page on the Toyota 2000GT and its pages on the Nissan S30 and Z-car, a March twenty twenty-one report by MotorPress, BusinessDay in South Africa, Toyota's UK magazine, Classic and Sports Car, Hagerty, Shannons Club and Sports Car Market. They disagree on names, dates and counts, and we show the disagreements. Our own arithmetic is labelled.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT, NISSAN S30, NISSAN Z) · MOTORPRESS (8 MAR 2021) · BUSINESSDAY SA (18 OCT 2022) · TOYOTA UK MAGAZINE (2012) · CLASSIC & SPORTS CAR (MAR 2022) · HAGERTY · SHANNONS · SCM · DISAGREEMENTS SHOWN

scenes.text: The MotorPress report sets the scene. In the nineteen sixties, it says, Japanese cars were widely seen as inferior to Western cars in quality, performance and reliability, even though they were growing in popularity and often proved more reliable than American and European models. Japan had cars for most segments, but no luxury high-performance sports car.
scenes.caption: MOTORPRESS (8 MAR 2021): JAPANESE CARS SEEN AS INFERIOR IN QUALITY, PERFORMANCE, RELIABILITY · GROWING IN POPULARITY · OFTEN MORE RELIABLE THAN US / EUROPEAN CARS · NO LUXURY HIGH-PERFORMANCE SPORTS CAR
scenes.chapter: A country without a halo car

scenes.text: The benchmarks were abroad. MotorPress names the Jaguar E-Type, the Porsche 911, the Ferrari 250 GTO and the Corvette. It says Japan's first Grand Prix, in nineteen sixty-three, sparked local interest in performance, and that about a year later Toyota started a luxury performance project. By our arithmetic, that places the start around nineteen sixty-four.
scenes.caption: MOTORPRESS: BENCHMARKS — JAGUAR E-TYPE, PORSCHE 911, FERRARI 250 GTO, CORVETTE · JAPAN'S FIRST GRAND PRIX 1963 · TOYOTA PROJECT ~1 YEAR LATER → ~1964 (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Wikipedia gives Toyota's reasoning. It says Toyota saw that top sports or grand touring coupés drew customers into showrooms, and felt the engine of its Sports 800 was too small for a world-class sports car. Yamaha would later offer a design that Toyota accepted, Wikipedia says, to improve its conservative image.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): TOP SPORTS / GT COUPÉS DREW CUSTOMERS INTO SHOWROOMS · SPORTS 800 ENGINE 'TOO SMALL' FOR A WORLD-CLASS SPORTS CAR · YAMAHA'S DESIGN ACCEPTED 'TO IMPROVE ITS CONSERVATIVE IMAGE'

scenes.text: The car did not begin at Toyota. Wikipedia says the motorcycle and engine maker Yamaha set up a Technical Research Institute in nineteen fifty-nine and built a sports car called the YX30, a sixteen hundred cubic centimetre four-cylinder inspired by an MG engine. It closed the institute in nineteen sixty-two.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): YAMAHA TECHNICAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE 1959 · YX30, 1,600 CC 4-CYL, 'INSPIRED BY THE MG B-SERIES DOHC' · INSTITUTE CLOSED 1962

scenes.text: Then came a prototype called the A550X. Wikipedia's page on the Toyota says Nissan cancelled that project and launched its Silvia coupé in nineteen sixty-five. The Nissan Z page tells it differently: Nissan and Yamaha made a prototype in nineteen sixty-one, and Nissan scrapped it by nineteen sixty-four because Yamaha's twin-cam engine did not meet its expectations.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): A550X BUILT; NISSAN CANCELLED; NISSAN LAUNCHED SILVIA COUPÉ 1965 · WIKIPEDIA (NISSAN Z): YX-30 PROTOTYPE 1961; SCRAPPED BY 1964; YAMAHA DOHC 2.0 L 'DID NOT MEET EXPECTATIONS' → DATES AND NAMES DIFFER BETWEEN PAGES

scenes.text: The sources also disagree on the order. Shannons Club says Nissan hired the German designer Albrecht Goertz from May nineteen sixty-three, and that his A550X prototype carried many 240Z styling themes. MotorPress says Yamaha's prototype was developed for Nissan, which turned it down, and that Nissan later used elements of it for the 240Z.
scenes.caption: SHANNONS: GOERTZ CONSULTED BY NISSAN FROM MAY 1963; A550X ≈ 240Z STYLING THEMES; THEN HE MOVED TO TOYOTA · MOTORPRESS: YAMAHA'S PROTOTYPE FOR NISSAN REJECTED; NISSAN LATER USED ELEMENTS FOR 240Z · HAGERTY: GOERTZ CREDIT DISPUTE

scenes.text: Hagerty adds a bitter footnote. It says Goertz's later dispute over design credit reportedly led to a threatened lawsuit. It does not say what happened next, and neither does any other source we read. We can say the A550X is named in several of them, that Nissan rejected it, and that Toyota took its place.
scenes.caption: HAGERTY: GOERTZ DISPUTE OVER DESIGN CREDIT → THREATENED LAWSUIT (OUTCOME NOT GIVEN) · A550X NAMED BY WIKIPEDIA, SHANNONS, HAGERTY · MOTORPRESS CALLS IT 'A55X'

scenes.text: MotorPress names the man who ran the project: Shoichi Saito, described as a major contributor to Toyota's development. His brief, abridged, was to do whatever was necessary to not only produce the 2000GT but make it one of the best. The design goals were a practical, fun-to-drive front-engined, rear-wheel-drive car with styling to rival costlier European cars.
scenes.caption: MOTORPRESS: PROJECT LEADER SHOICHI SAITO · BRIEF (ABRIDGED): 'DO WHATEVER NECESSARY TO NOT ONLY PRODUCE THE 2000GT, BUT MAKE IT ONE OF THE BEST' · GOALS: PRACTICAL, FUN, FRONT ENGINE RWD, STYLING TO RIVAL PRICIER EUROPEANS

scenes.text: The designers are named differently. MotorPress credits Toyota designers Jiro Kawano and Satoru Nozaki, who developed the Yamaha prototype into the 280 A1. Wikipedia's infobox lists Jiro Kono as product manager and Satoru Nozaki as designer. The two spellings, Kawano and Kono, may be the same person, but neither source says so.
scenes.caption: MOTORPRESS: JIRO KAWANO + SATORU NOZAKI · WIKIPEDIA INFOBOX: JIRO KONO (SHUSA / PRODUCT MANAGER) + SATORU NOZAKI (DESIGNER) · KAWANO = KONO? NOT STATED

scenes.text: Wikipedia is inconsistent about the design itself. Its body text says most of the design work was done by Yamaha, but also says Toyota used a design from its own designer, Nozaki. Nozaki's styling was reportedly inspired by the Jaguar E-Type. The page does not settle who drew the final car, and neither do we.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): 'MOST DESIGN WORK DONE BY YAMAHA' AND 'TOYOTA USED NOZAKI'S DESIGN' · NOZAKI STYLING 'REPORTEDLY INSPIRED BY' E-TYPE · FINAL AUTHORSHIP: UNRESOLVED IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The timeline of the first car is also loosely documented. Wikipedia says the first prototype was built in August nineteen sixty-five, eleven months after the project began. By our arithmetic, that puts the start around September nineteen sixty-four. Classic and Sports Car says Project two eighty A began in the summer of nineteen sixty-four, which is close.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: FIRST PROTOTYPE AUG 1965, 11 MONTHS AFTER PROJECT BEGAN → ~SEP 1964 (OUR ARITHMETIC) · C&SC: PROJECT 280A BEGAN SUMMER 1964

scenes.text: The car was shown at the nineteen sixty-five Tokyo Motor Show, as the 280 A1 according to MotorPress, about a year after Saito commissioned it. Wikipedia says production vehicles took about two years more to appear, with production running from May nineteen sixty-seven to August nineteen seventy at Yamaha's Iwata factory in Shizuoka.
scenes.caption: MOTORPRESS: 280 A1 AT 1965 TOKYO MOTOR SHOW · WIKIPEDIA: PRODUCTION CARS ~2 YEARS LATER; PRODUCTION MAY 1967 – AUG 1970 AT YAMAHA'S IWATA, SHIZUOKA FACTORY

scenes.text: A quick timeline, from our sources. Yamaha opened its research institute in nineteen fifty-nine. Japan held its first Grand Prix in nineteen sixty-three. Toyota's project began around nineteen sixty-four, the prototype was built in August nineteen sixty-five, and production began in May nineteen sixty-seven. By our arithmetic, that is eight years from the institute to the first production car.
scenes.caption: 1959 YAMAHA INSTITUTE · 1963 JAPAN'S FIRST GP (MOTORPRESS) · ~1964 TOYOTA PROJECT · AUG 1965 PROTOTYPE · MAY 1967 PRODUCTION (WIKIPEDIA) · 1959 → 1967 = 8 YEARS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: And from prototype to showroom, Wikipedia says about two years. By our arithmetic, August nineteen sixty-five to May nineteen sixty-seven is twenty-one months. Production then lasted thirty-nine months, to August nineteen seventy. So the car spent more than half as long in development as it did on sale, a ratio our sources never mention but which the dates make plain.
scenes.caption: AUG 1965 → MAY 1967 = 21 MONTHS · MAY 1967 → AUG 1970 = 39 MONTHS · 21 ÷ 39 = 54% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · WIKIPEDIA: 'ABOUT TWO YEARS' · RATIO NOT STATED BY ANY SOURCE

scenes.text: The engine came from a Toyota Crown. Wikipedia says the one thousand nine hundred eighty-eight cubic centimetre 3M straight six started with the Crown's S50 engine, and Yamaha fitted a new twin-cam head and three Mikuni-Solex carburettors, for one hundred fifty metric horsepower at sixty-six hundred revs. Nine cars, the MF12, used a two point three litre engine rated at one hundred forty.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): 1,988 CC 3M FROM CROWN S50 + YAMAHA DOHC HEAD + 3 MIKUNI-SOLEX 40 PHH · 150 PS @ 6,600 RPM · 9 MF12 WITH 2.3 L 2M-B SOHC, 140 PS

scenes.text: Standard equipment was advanced for the time. Wikipedia lists a limited-slip differential, power-assisted disc brakes on all four wheels and rack-and-pinion steering, the first on a Toyota, and calls it the first Japanese car with four-wheel disc brakes. MotorPress and BusinessDay add an aluminium body and make a similar claim of a first for the disc brakes and differential.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: LSD · 4-WHEEL POWER-ASSISTED DISCS · RACK-AND-PINION (FIRST ON A TOYOTA) · 'FIRST JAPANESE CAR WITH 4-WHEEL DISCS' · MOTORPRESS + BUSINESSDAY: ALUMINIUM BODY; FIRST JAPANESE CAR WITH LSD + POWER DISCS (THEIR CLAIM) · 'FIRST' CLAIMS NOT INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED

scenes.text: Performance claims vary. BusinessDay and MotorPress give one hundred ten kilowatts, zero to one hundred in about ten seconds and two hundred fifteen kilometres an hour. By our arithmetic, that is one hundred thirty-four miles an hour, close to Wikipedia's claimed one hundred thirty-five. MotorPress adds that for its power, the car's performance was impressive, but it struggled against the E-Type and Corvette.
scenes.caption: BUSINESSDAY / MOTORPRESS: 110 KW · 175 NM · 0–100 KM/H ~10 S · 215 KM/H (= 133.6 MPH, OUR ARITHMETIC) · WIKIPEDIA: 135 MPH CLAIMED · MOTORPRESS: 'STRUGGLED AGAINST THE E-TYPE AND CORVETTE'

scenes.text: Road and Track, MotorPress says, praised the car as one of the most exciting it had driven and compared it with the Porsche 911. That is a magazine opinion, quoted second-hand, with no date or test figures in our source. We use it as colour, not as proof of speed.
scenes.caption: MOTORPRESS: ROAD & TRACK — 'ONE OF THE MOST EXCITING CARS IT HAD DRIVEN'; COMPARED WITH THE 911 · DATE AND TEST FIGURES: NOT GIVEN → SECOND-HAND OPINION

scenes.text: The proving ground was the Yatabe High Speed Test Track. Wikipedia says that in nineteen sixty-six a 2000GT set thirteen FIA world speed and endurance records in a seventy-two-hour test. BusinessDay and MotorPress both repeat the seventy-two hours. By our arithmetic, that is three days and nights of continuous running in a single test.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (2000GT): 1966, YATABE HIGH SPEED TEST TRACK — 13 FIA WORLD SPEED + ENDURANCE RECORDS IN 72 HOURS · BUSINESSDAY + MOTORPRESS: 72-HOUR TEST · 72 H = 3 DAYS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: There is a dramatic ending. Wikipedia says the record car was destroyed in a pace-car accident and later scrapped. It also says the records prompted Porsche to prepare a nine-eleven R to beat them. Our sources do not give the individual records, speeds, drivers or the car's total distance, so the headline is all we have.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: RECORD CAR DESTROYED IN A PACE-CAR ACCIDENT, LATER SCRAPPED · RECORDS 'PROMPTED PORSCHE TO PREPARE A 911R TO BEAT THEM' · INDIVIDUAL RECORDS / SPEEDS / DRIVERS / DISTANCE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Wikipedia adds a final twist about a replica. It says Toyota later took back one of the Shelby race cars and rebuilt it as a replica of the record car, and that it remains in Japan. The same sentence says Shelby entered a pair of cars, then says he built three, including a spare. The page leaves that count unresolved.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: TOYOTA TOOK BACK ONE SHELBY CAR, REBUILT AS A REPLICA OF THE RECORD CAR; REMAINS IN JAPAN · SHELBY CARS: 'A PAIR' vs 3 BUILT INCLUDING A SPARE · C&SC: 3 CARS (10001, 10005, 10006)

scenes.text: The racing record is from Wikipedia. A third place at the nineteen sixty-six Japanese Grand Prix at Fuji. The first win at the inaugural Suzuka one thousand kilometres in nineteen sixty-six. And in nineteen sixty-seven, wins at the twenty-four hours of Fuji and the Fuji one thousand kilometres. By our arithmetic, that is three wins and a podium in two seasons.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 1966 JAPANESE GP (FUJI) 3RD · 1966 SUZUKA 1000 KM — WIN · 1967 24 HOURS OF FUJI — WIN · 1967 FUJI 1000 KM — WIN · 3 WINS + 1 PODIUM IN 2 SEASONS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Then America. Classic and Sports Car says the Shelby team ran three Toyota-Shelby cars in the nineteen sixty-eight SCCA championship, driven by Dave Jordan and Scooter Patrick. The cars finished fourth in the National Championship with four wins, eight seconds and six thirds. The Shelby program lasted one season, and our sources do not explain why.
scenes.caption: C&SC: 3 TOYOTA-SHELBY CARS, 1968 SCCA · DRIVERS DAVE JORDAN + SCOOTER PATRICK · 4TH IN NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP · 4 WINS + 8 SECONDS + 6 THIRDS · ONE SEASON (WIKIPEDIA) · REASON IT ENDED: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Toyota's racing did not end there. Wikipedia says the Toyota Seven, the company's first purpose-built racing car, was developed from lessons learned on the 2000GT. That is a single line, with no engineering detail. But it frames the 2000GT as more than a showpiece: it was a test bed for what Toyota built next.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: TOYOTA 7 = TOYOTA'S FIRST PURPOSE-BUILT RACING CAR, 'DEVELOPED FROM LESSONS LEARNED ON THE 2000GT' · NO ENGINEERING DETAIL GIVEN

scenes.text: The first car off the line has a recorded history. Classic and Sports Car says the Toyota-Shelby chassis ten thousand one was the first serial-numbered car, built on the twenty-seventh of September nineteen sixty-six in Solar Red. By our arithmetic, that is eight months before Wikipedia's May nineteen sixty-seven start of production, which our sources do not explain.
scenes.caption: C&SC: MF10-10001 = FIRST SERIAL-NUMBERED CAR, BUILT 27 SEP 1966, SOLAR RED · WIKIPEDIA: PRODUCTION FROM MAY 1967 · 27 SEP 1966 → MAY 1967 ≈ 7–8 MONTHS (OUR ARITHMETIC) · EXPLANATION: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: That car later sold. At Gooding's Amelia Island sale on the fourth of March twenty twenty-two it made two million five hundred thirty-five thousand dollars, below an estimate of two point seven five to three point five million, per Classic and Sports Car. Hagerty called it the record for a Japanese car at auction, passing the Mazda 767B. Fifty-five years and a few months after it was built, it became the car's price peak.
scenes.caption: C&SC: $2,535,000, 4 MAR 2022; ESTIMATE $2.75–3.5 M · HAGERTY: RECORD FOR A JAPANESE CAR AT AUCTION · SEP 1966 → MAR 2022 = 55 YEARS 5 MONTHS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Then the film. The 2000GT appeared in You Only Live Twice in nineteen sixty-seven. Wikipedia says two one-off topless cars were built. MotorPress and BusinessDay say two convertibles were commissioned because of Sean Connery's size and the small cabin, and that Toyota removed the roof and fitted a soft top.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: TWO ONE-OFF TOPLESS MODELS WITH TONNEAU COVERS · MOTORPRESS + BUSINESSDAY: TWO CONVERTIBLES BECAUSE OF CONNERY'S SIZE AND SMALL CABIN; ROOF REMOVED, SOFT TOP FITTED

scenes.text: Wikipedia adds detail. A targa roof was reportedly considered for Connery, who is one point eight eight metres tall, and a roofless version was reportedly built in under two weeks. Akiko Wakabayashi's character, Aki, was the only person to drive the car in the film. Both claims are marked as reported, so we pass them on with that caution.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: TARGA CONSIDERED FOR CONNERY (1.88 M); ROOFLESS VERSION 'REPORTEDLY BUILT IN UNDER TWO WEEKS' · AKIKO WAKABAYASHI'S CHARACTER AKI WAS THE ONLY ONE TO DRIVE IT IN THE FILM · 'REPORTED' CLAIMS

scenes.text: Our sources do not give the film cars' build cost, who did the work, or where the cars are. Many online stories fill those gaps, but we could not verify them. One last note from Wikipedia: Daniel Craig is said to call it his favourite Bond car. Wikipedia does not date the remark, so we leave it as an unverified quote.
scenes.caption: BUILD COST, BUILDER, CURRENT LOCATION OF FILM CARS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · DANIEL CRAIG 'FAVOURITE BOND CAR' (WIKIPEDIA, UNDATED) → UNVERIFIED QUOTE

scenes.text: Now the commercial story. Wikipedia says a 2000GT in America listed for about seven thousand one hundred fifty dollars in nineteen sixty-eight, which it converts to roughly sixty-six thousand one hundred ninety-seven in twenty twenty-five dollars. That put it above the E-Type at five thousand five hundred thirty-nine and the Porsche 911S at six thousand seven hundred ninety.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 1968 US PRICE ~$7,150 ≈ $66,197 IN 2025 DOLLARS · E-TYPE $5,539 · 911S $6,790 · FERRARI 365 GTB/4 $19,700 · SCM: ORIGINAL LIST $6,800 (CONFLICT)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, in today's money the Toyota cost about nine times its nineteen sixty-eight sticker, and the Ferrari 365 GTB/4 at nineteen thousand seven hundred would be roughly one hundred eighty thousand under the same conversion. That Ferrari figure is our own extension of Wikipedia's ratio, since the page converts only the Toyota's price.
scenes.caption: 66,197 ÷ 7,150 = 9.26× · 19,700 × 9.26 = $182,400 (OUR ARITHMETIC, APPLYING WIKIPEDIA'S TOYOTA RATIO TO THE FERRARI; NOT A SOURCED CONVERSION)

scenes.text: Few people bought it. Wikipedia says about sixty cars reached North America, sales were weak, and Toyota is believed to have made no profit, which led to cancellation in nineteen seventy. Classic and Sports Car says Toyota had hoped to build a thousand a year and built three hundred fifty-one. By our arithmetic, that is nine cars a month over production.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: ~60 TO NORTH AMERICA · WEAK SALES → CANCELLED 1970 · 'BELIEVED' NO PROFIT · C&SC: HOPED 1,000/YEAR; BUILT 351 · 351 ÷ 39 MONTHS = 9.0/MONTH (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The count of cars remains disputed. Wikipedia's infobox gives three hundred fifty-one, its body text three hundred thirty-seven regular units, all reportedly sold, and Sports Car Market three hundred fifty-four. MotorPress and BusinessDay both say three hundred fifty-one. The Japanese Nostalgic Car website, in twenty fourteen, said three hundred thirty-seven.
scenes.caption: 351: WIKIPEDIA INFOBOX, MOTORPRESS, BUSINESSDAY, C&SC · 337: WIKIPEDIA BODY TEXT, JAPANESE NOSTALGIC CAR (2014) · 354: SCM · NO RECONCILIATION · 351 − 337 = 14 (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: What replaced it? Wikipedia says Toyota and Yamaha later built the sixteen hundred GT, based on the Corona hardtop coupé with a Yamaha-developed twin-cam head. The Celica replaced the 2000GT as the top model at Toyota Corolla Store dealerships. MotorPress says the car influenced later Toyota sports cars including the Supra, the GT86 and the Lexus LFA.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 1600GT (COROLLA-BASED COUPÉ, YAMAHA DOHC HEAD) · CELICA REPLACED 2000GT AS TOP MODEL AT COROLLA STORE · MOTORPRESS: INFLUENCED SUPRA, GT86, LEXUS LFA (ARTICLE'S CLAIM; NO DETAIL)

scenes.text: For years, the market did not care. Sports Car Market records two cars that failed to sell in nineteen ninety-two at sixty thousand and forty-two thousand five hundred dollars. By August nineteen ninety-eight, one sold for seventy-seven thousand five hundred. In two thousand six, two hundred twenty-five thousand six hundred. In August two thousand twelve, six hundred twenty-seven thousand.
scenes.caption: SCM: 1992 NO-SALES AT $60,000 + $42,500 · AUG 1998 $77,500 · JUL 2006 $225,600 · AUG 2012 $627,000

scenes.text: The first million came in Fort Worth on the twenty-seventh of April twenty thirteen, one million one hundred fifty-five thousand dollars, a record for a Japanese car per Sports Car Market. Hagerty later confirmed the Mazda 767B passed it at one point seven five million in twenty seventeen, and then the Toyota-Shelby retook the record at two point five three five million in twenty twenty-two.
scenes.caption: SCM: 27 APR 2013 $1,155,000 (RM FORT WORTH) · HAGERTY: MAZDA 767B $1.75 M (AMELIA 2017) · TOYOTA-SHELBY $2.535 M (GOODING AMELIA ISLAND, 4 MAR 2022) — RECORD FOR A JAPANESE CAR AT AUCTION

scenes.text: Hagerty's valuation page today shows eight hundred forty-four thousand dollars for a good nineteen sixty-seven car, down one point one percent in twelve months. By our arithmetic, that is twelve point seven times the nineteen sixty-eight price in inflation-adjusted terms and one hundred eighteen times in nominal dollars. The car that cost Toyota money has become one of the most valuable Japanese cars ever made.
scenes.caption: HAGERTY (1967 PAGE): $844,000 'GOOD, AVERAGE SPEC'; −1.1% IN 12 MONTHS · 844,000 ÷ 66,197 = 12.7× (REAL) · 844,000 ÷ 7,150 = 118× (NOMINAL) (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: There is a restoration movement too. In July twenty twenty, Toyota's Gazoo Racing announced the GR Heritage Parts Project, which reproduces replacement parts for the 2000GT, according to BusinessDay. Toyota South Africa then began a full bumper-to-bumper restoration of its own car in twenty twenty, which took about two years, BusinessDay says.
scenes.caption: BUSINESSDAY + MOTORPRESS: TOYOTA GAZOO RACING GR HERITAGE PARTS PROJECT, ANNOUNCED JULY (BUSINESSDAY: 2020); WIKIPEDIA ALSO MENTIONS THE PROGRAM · TOYOTA SOUTH AFRICA RESTORATION BEGAN 2020, ~2 YEARS · PART PRICES + RESTORATION COST: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Nissan's answer to the 2000GT is part of this story. Shannons says Toyota sold few cars but gained publicity, and that this pushed Nissan to take the Goertz prototype toward production. The Datsun 240Z was shown on the eighteenth of October nineteen sixty-nine. Wikipedia says over forty-five thousand were sold in the United States through the nineteen seventy-one model year.
scenes.caption: SHANNONS: TOYOTA 'SOLD FEW BUT GAINED PUBLICITY' → NISSAN PUSHED PROTOTYPE TO PRODUCTION · 240Z SHOWN 18 OCT 1969 · WIKIPEDIA (S30): 45,000+ US SALES THROUGH MY1971

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, that is more than one hundred twenty-eight Datsuns for every Toyota in just the first few years, counting the 351. Over the 240Z's whole American run through nineteen seventy-three the figure passes three hundred eighty-five. Shannons calls the 240Z the best-selling sports car in the world. The Toyota did not win on sales, but it started the race.
scenes.caption: 45,000 ÷ 351 = 128× · (45 + 50 + 40) THOUSAND ÷ 351 = 385× (OUR ARITHMETIC; 'OVER' FIGURES = MINIMUMS) · SHANNONS: 240Z 'BEST-SELLING SPORTS CAR IN THE WORLD' · 'STARTED THE RACE' = OUR PHRASE

scenes.text: Toyota's UK magazine tells how one car came back. It was first registered in Mozambique, found in Portugal in twenty eleven, and first listed for sale on eBay. JD Classics restored it, with the engine rebuilt by the specialist Piff over an estimated two hundred fifty to three hundred hours, and new pistons made by a NASCAR company in America.
scenes.caption: TOYOTA UK MAGAZINE (6 DEC 2012): ORIGINALLY MOZAMBIQUE; FOUND IN PORTUGAL 2011; LISTED ON EBAY · JD CLASSICS RESTORATION · ENGINE BY PIFF 250–300 H · PISTONS BY A NASCAR COMPANY · FINAL PRICE PAID: NOT DISCLOSED

scenes.text: Another car nearly did not survive. Japanese Nostalgic Car reported in June twenty fourteen that a 2000GT in Japan had been crushed by a falling beech tree, and that the owner had decided to rebuild it. The article gives no repair cost, and its comments, which guessed at half a million dollars, are unverified. We do not know whether the rebuild was finished.
scenes.caption: JAPANESE NOSTALGIC CAR (19 JUN 2014): 2000GT CRUSHED BY AN AGED BEECH TREE; OWNER TO REBUILD · NO COST GIVEN · COMMENTS' $500,000 GUESS UNVERIFIED · OUTCOME: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: One car tells the story at small scale. MotorPress says only three of the three hundred fifty-one were destined for South Africa: chassis ten thousand one hundred thirty-one and two hundred six in Pegasus White, and chassis two hundred seven in Thunder Silver, arriving between nineteen sixty-seven and nineteen sixty-eight. By our arithmetic, that is under one percent of production.
scenes.caption: MOTORPRESS: MF10-10131 (PEGASUS WHITE) · MF10-10206 (PEGASUS WHITE) · MF10-10207 (THUNDER SILVER) · ARRIVED 1967–68 · 3 ÷ 351 = 0.85% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Toyota South Africa has owned chassis two hundred seven for many years, MotorPress says, as part of its private collection. BusinessDay says it is the only survivor of the three and has thirty thousand kilometres on the odometer. The colour is a puzzle: some sources say Thunder Silver, others white, and the car is now painted Solar Red from a previous owner.
scenes.caption: MOTORPRESS: TOYOTA SA OWNS MF10-10207 · BUSINESSDAY: ONLY SURVIVOR OF 3; 30,000 KM · COLOUR: THUNDER SILVER vs WHITE (SOURCES CONFLICT); NOW SOLAR RED, FROM A PREVIOUS OWNER'S RESPRAY (BUSINESSDAY: ORIGINALLY SILVER)

scenes.text: BusinessDay values it at about thirty million rand, with pristine cars reaching forty million at auction. MotorPress says pristine examples sell for just under fifteen million rand. These two numbers conflict, and the articles are nineteen months apart. We do not convert currencies, because we have no rate, and we show both.
scenes.caption: BUSINESSDAY (OCT 2022): ~R30 M VALUE; PRISTINE UP TO R40 M · MOTORPRESS (MAR 2021): PRISTINE 'JUST UNDER R15 M' · CONFLICT · 19 MONTHS APART (MAR 2021 → OCT 2022) (OUR ARITHMETIC) · NO CURRENCY CONVERSION

scenes.text: MotorPress calls the 2000GT the first million-dollar Japanese car but gives no source, and our sources show the million came with the Fort Worth sale in twenty thirteen. A seven-figure sale is no longer rare. Classic and Sports Car says the 2000GT holds the top eighteen Toyota auction prices. No other Toyota model appears on that list.
scenes.caption: MOTORPRESS: 'FIRST MILLION-DOLLAR JAPANESE CAR' (UNSOURCED) · SCM: $1,155,000 ON 27 APR 2013 (RECORD) · HAGERTY: 'FIRST SEVEN-FIGURE JAPANESE CLASSIC' = A DIFFERENT 2000GT, 9 YEARS BEFORE 2022 · C&SC: 2000GTs HOLD TOP 18 TOYOTA AUCTION PRICES

scenes.text: So here is the insane part of the story, in order. A car designed for one company, rejected, and handed to another. Built by a motorcycle maker. Priced above a Porsche. Sold in numbers measured in hundreds. Unprofitable. Cancelled. And then, fifty years later, one of the most valuable Japanese cars in the world.
scenes.caption: DESIGNED FOR NISSAN → REJECTED → TOYOTA · BUILT BY YAMAHA · PRICED ABOVE PORSCHE 911S ($7,150 vs $6,790) · 351 BUILT · NO PROFIT · CANCELLED 1970 · $2.535 M IN 2022

scenes.text: The story in numbers. Thirteen records in seventy-two hours. Three hundred fifty-one cars, give or take the disputed counts. About sixty sent to North America, which by our arithmetic is seventeen percent of the total. A price of seven thousand one hundred fifty dollars in nineteen sixty-eight, and two million five hundred thirty-five thousand for the best car in twenty twenty-two.
scenes.caption: 13 RECORDS · 72 HOURS · 351 BUILT (337 / 354 DISPUTED) · ~60 TO NORTH AMERICA = 60 ÷ 351 = 17% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · $7,150 (1968) · $2,535,000 (2022)

scenes.text: What did it teach Toyota? Our sources give a modest answer. Wikipedia says the car inspired later sporty Toyotas and fed into the Toyota Seven racing car. MotorPress lists the Supra, the GT86 and the Lexus LFA as descendants. None of these claims is detailed, so treat them as the articles' own judgement, not engineering history we have verified.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: INSPIRED LATER SPORTY TOYOTAS; TOYOTA 7 'DEVELOPED FROM LESSONS' · MOTORPRESS: SUPRA, GT86, LEXUS LFA · NO DETAIL → ARTICLES' JUDGEMENT, NOT VERIFIED ENGINEERING LINEAGE

scenes.text: Here is what we could not confirm. The exact origin story, since two Wikipedia pages and several articles tell it differently. Who drew the final car. The individual Yatabe records. Why the Shelby program ended after a year. The film cars' cost and fate. The true production count. And any independent test of the car's speed. We have flagged each one.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES / CONFLICTING: ORIGIN STORY (YX-30 1961 vs 1959–62 INSTITUTE) · FINAL DESIGN AUTHORSHIP · YATABE RECORD DETAILS · WHY SHELBY ENDED · FILM CAR COST + FATE · PRODUCTION COUNT (337 / 351 / 354) · INDEPENDENT SPEED TEST
scenes.chapter: What the sources do not say

scenes.text: That is the story of the Toyota 2000GT: a car built to prove that Japan could build a supercar, which proved it and lost money doing so. If you enjoyed this, subscribe to Pickup Reality, and tell us which exotic car's story you want us to check next. Every source is in the description.
